title: Cold Chain & Food Traceability RFID — FSMA 204, Reefer Temperature Logging & EUDR Provenance
summary: Food producers, processors, distributors and retailers use UHF and HF RFID — including sensor-enabled UCODE 9xe and EM4325 temperature-logging chips — to satisfy FDA Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) section 204 (the Food Traceability Final Rule, compliance date January 2026), the FDA Food Traceability List (FTL), GS1 EPCIS event traceability, EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR, December 2025) provenance traceability, vaccine cold-chain (CDC VFC and WHO PQS), and reefer-container temperature audit trails. Proud Tek supplies frozen-food labels (cryogenic-rated adhesive, -30 °C survivable), reefer-container UHF tags, sensor-enabled UHF temperature loggers and the encoding services that link physical tags into GS1 EPCIS / GDST seafood-traceability backends.
heroPoints: FSMA 204 Food Traceability Final Rule ready. Compliance date January 20, 2026 for all FTL-listed foods; GS1 EPCIS event capture supported via pre-encoded SGTIN-96 and GTIN+lot tag encoding.

Reefer / cold-chain temperature logging. Sensor-enabled UCODE 9xe and EM4325 UHF chips capture temperature events in-tag and report at every read for HACCP, vaccine cold chain and pharma cold-chain audit trails.

EUDR provenance ready — Dec 30, 2025 EU Deforestation Regulation requires geo-located provenance for cocoa, coffee, cattle, palm, soy, rubber, timber and derived products; RFID + EPCIS event capture is the recommended carrier.

sections.title: Challenges food and cold-chain operators face without RFID traceability
bullets: FSMA 204 critical-tracking-event (CTE) data capture is required by January 2026 for every food on the FDA Food Traceability List (FTL): leafy greens, herbs, sprouts, melons, peppers, tomatoes, tropical tree fruits, fresh-cut produce, shell eggs, nut butters, fresh / frozen / smoked finfish & crustaceans, ready-to-eat deli salads and soft cheeses; processors capturing CTEs by paper or spreadsheet face audit-finding risk and the operational burden of manual CTE filing across thousands of receiving and shipping events per day.

Reefer-container temperature excursions undetected for hours. A -25 °C frozen-protein container that warms to -10 °C for 6-12 hours during a refrigeration outage may be completely undetected without active temperature logging; the resulting product loss claim is typically $40,000-$120,000 per container with the manufacturer / 3PL / carrier all denying responsibility.

Vaccine cold-chain failure under CDC VFC. The CDC Vaccines for Children program requires continuous temperature monitoring with documented response procedures; a single VFC enrollment with documented cold-chain failure faces program disenrollment and reputational damage.

EUDR provenance for cocoa, coffee, cattle, palm, soy, rubber and timber from December 30, 2025 — products entering the EU market must carry geo-located provenance proving no association with land deforested after Dec 31, 2020; without unit-level RFID + EPCIS event capture, importers cannot satisfy the due-diligence statement requirement.

GDST seafood-traceability standard adoption. Major seafood retailers (Walmart, Tesco, Carrefour, Coles, Loblaws) are progressively requiring GDST 1.1 traceability for seafood; processors without unit-level traceability lose shelf-space access in tier-1 retail.

Recall scope without unit-level traceability. A Listeria outbreak traced to a single processing line on a single shift requires unit-level recall scoping; without RFID-enabled traceability, the recall expands to the entire plant's output for that week and the cost-of-recall multiplies 10-50x.

bullets: Frozen-food RFID labels rated to -30 °C — cryogenic adhesive, low-temperature substrate and freezer-tunnel applicator-compatible release liner; survives the deep-freeze tunnel, frozen storage and thaw cycle without delamination or read-rate degradation.

Sensor-enabled UHF temperature loggers. UCODE 9xe self-tunes for temperature compensation; EM4325 captures temperature on-tag with battery-assisted passive (BAP) operation for up to 5 years of in-container event capture, with sensor reads on every UHF inventory query.

Reefer-container on-metal UHF tags. Slim ceramic on-metal tags applied to the reefer chassis; portal readers at the loading dock and at port-of-entry capture the container ID and link it to the temperature-log record.

Pre-encoded GS1 SGTIN-96 + GTIN/lot encoding. Proud Tek pre-encodes the EPC tag memory to GS1 EPCIS-ready SGTIN-96 plus optional lot-and-expiration data so the physical tag drops directly into the customer's TraceLink, FoodLogiQ, ConnectingFoodIndustry or IBM Food Trust EPCIS event-capture pipeline.

Pharmaceutical-grade vial labels for vaccine cold chain. UHF labels with cryogenic adhesive for -70 °C ultra-cold-chain (mRNA vaccine) and -20 °C standard cold-chain (most other vaccines) deployments, supporting CDC VFC and WHO PQS PQ-prequalified cold-chain monitoring.

Tier-1 seafood processor adopted GDST 1.1 traceability with Proud Tek pre-encoded UHF case labels and retained shelf access at three major retailers that imposed mid-2025 traceability cutoffs on uncertified suppliers.

Cocoa importer to EU (preparing for EUDR Dec 2025) deployed Proud Tek RFID at first-receipt and tied tag-EPC to plot-level GPS provenance; due-diligence statement file size dropped from gigabytes of PDFs (previous flow) to a structured EPCIS event log.

faq.question: Is RFID required by FSMA 204?
faq.answer: FSMA 204 requires Critical Tracking Event (CTE) data capture for foods on the Food Traceability List, but does not mandate a specific data-carrier technology. Barcodes, RFID, manual entry and EDI are all permissible. RFID is the recommended carrier for high-volume processing lines because it captures CTEs automatically without slowing throughput; large processors are deploying RFID + GS1 EPCIS as the de-facto FSMA 204 architecture.

faq.question: What is a sensor-enabled UHF chip and when do I need one?
faq.answer: Sensor-enabled UHF chips (NXP UCODE 9xe, EM Microelectronic EM4325) include temperature sensing on the chip die. UCODE 9xe is fully passive and captures the temperature at the moment of read; EM4325 is battery-assisted passive (BAP) and captures temperature events autonomously for up to 5 years between reads. Choose sensor-enabled chips when continuous in-container temperature logging is required for audit (reefer, vaccine, blood bank). Passive read-only chips cannot capture mid-shipment excursions.

faq.question: Can RFID labels survive frozen-tunnel application?
faq.answer: Yes — but only with the right adhesive and substrate. Proud Tek frozen-food labels use cryogenic-rated permanent acrylic adhesive that bonds at -30 °C and survives the deep-freeze tunnel, frozen storage and the eventual thaw without delamination. Standard pressure-sensitive labels fail at the freezer-tunnel application step; only specifically cryogenic-rated formulations work in this application.

faq.question: Does Proud Tek encode tags to GS1 EPCIS / GDST format?
faq.answer: Yes. Proud Tek pre-encodes EPC tag memory to GS1 SGTIN-96 plus optional GTIN+lot+expiration data, ready to drop into TraceLink, FoodLogiQ, ConnectingFoodIndustry, IBM Food Trust or any GS1 EPCIS 2.0-compliant traceability platform. For GDST seafood, we provide the GDST 1.1 KDE (Key Data Element) encoding pattern as part of the encoding spec.

faq.question: What about vaccine cold chain at -70 °C (mRNA vaccines)?
faq.answer: Yes — Proud Tek supplies UHF medication-vial labels rated for -70 °C ultra-cold-chain (mRNA / cryogenic vaccine handling) plus the more common -20 °C standard cold chain. The label adhesive remains bonded through the cold-chain transit and the chip operates correctly through the entire temperature range. This supports CDC VFC and WHO PQS prequalified cold-chain monitoring deployments.
